# Failure Pattern Review FPR-2026-H1

**Site AUS-1 (fictional), Hall A.** Mar 2, 2026 to Aug 30, 2026 (26 weeks, 32 production racks). Prepared Sep 8, 2026; reviewed Sep 10, 2026 by the Customer Site Lead, IT Partner Site Manager, Landlord Chief Engineer. Interactive version: [Failure Pattern Review page](https://jasonmossotti.github.io/dco-vendor-scorecard/patterns/).

> A pattern means failures cluster beyond what chance explains. It is not proof of a bad batch or a careless partner until the cause is confirmed; the confidence of each cause is stated.

## Summary

Three patterns stand out from 496 failures in 26 weeks, and each has a different owner. A lot of optic modules is failing at 4.8 times the rate of the other lots; the Customer owns the supplier case and the IT Partner the replacements. Reseats of XID 79 faults do not hold (17 of 23 came back within 30 days), which is the IT Partner's to fix. The third pattern looked like the IT Partner's but was not: GPU thermal slowdowns in racks A17 to A24 followed CDU-A3's secondary supply temperature, which stayed under the 28.0 °C alarm the whole time, so no one on the Landlord's side was alerted. The rack with the most tickets, A11, is not a pattern; its 25 tickets are 8 unrelated kinds of failure.

| # | Pattern | Owner | Observed | Expected by chance | Rate vs. the rest | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | CDU-A3 ran warm for 48 days and the GPUs it cools throttled | Landlord | 20 trays | 2.0 | 25.8× | Confirmed: the slowdowns stopped when the filter was changed. |
| P2 | Optic lot LOT-2544 fails at 4.8 times the rate of the other lots | Customer (accountable), IT Partner (does the work) | 47 modules | 14.8 | 4.8× | Probable: the manufacturer's failure analysis is pending. |
| P3 | Reseats do not fix XID 79 faults | Customer (accountable), IT Partner (does the work) | 17 of 23 repairs came back | 1.7 | 9.9× | Confirmed by the recurrence data; the hardware cause is for the manufacturer. |

## P1. CDU-A3 ran warm for 48 days and the GPUs it cools throttled

*Signal:* GPU thermal slowdown · *Grouped by:* Racks a CDU serves, while it ran warm · *Failures:* May 27 to Jul 5 · *p* < 0.000001 (threshold 0.050) · *Owner (Interface Agreement RACI, CDUs and the hall secondary header):* Landlord

**What the data shows**

- CDU-A3 ran 1.0 °C or more above its 25.0 °C setpoint (daily mean) for 48 days, May 20 to Jul 6, peaking at 27.9 °C on Jun 29; its high-supply alarm is 28.0 °C, which it never reached. The other CDUs peaked at 26.0 °C.
- Secondary flow fell 5.1% (1,776 to 1,685 L/min, median).
- In the 8 racks it serves (A17 to A24), 20 trays had their first GPU thermal slowdown during that time, against 2.0 expected from the rest of the hall: 25.8× the rate.
- 22 of the hall's 34 thermal slowdowns in the 26 weeks happened in those racks while CDU-A3 ran warm; none of the other 12 happened where a CDU was running warm.
- The quarterly filter change on Jul 6 ended it; the racks had 2 thermal slowdowns in the 55 days after.
- Repairs while it ran warm: 14 tray replacements and 8 reseats.

**Root cause.** CDU-A3's filter fouled after its April 6 filter change. Secondary flow fell 5.1% and supply temperature crept up to a peak of 27.9 °C on June 29, just under the 28.0 °C high-supply alarm, so no alarm fired and the Landlord saw nothing to act on. The trays in the 8 racks it serves throttled: 20 trays had their first thermal slowdown while it ran warm, against 2.0 expected. The other CDUs never passed 26.0 °C. The quarterly filter change on July 6 restored the supply to setpoint, and the row then had only 2 thermal slowdowns in 55 days.

**Cost.** 22 tickets in the IT Partner's queue and 86 tray-hours out of service. 14 trays were replaced and 8 reseated for a cause that was on the Landlord's side of the rack manifold valves.

**Lesson.** A cooling problem can sit inside the alarm band and still cost capacity. Our fault attribution only looks for out-of-band coolant, so these outages were scored against the IT Partner, and every tray swap was the right call on the evidence the technician had.

**Standard-work changes**

| Document | Clause | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Interface Agreement | FA-1 | Attribute a capacity loss to the Landlord when the CDU secondary supply at the rack ran 1.0 °C or more above setpoint for 7 days, not only when it was out of band. |
| Landlord SLA | OT-CSL-03 | Add a deviation alarm: secondary supply 1.0 °C above setpoint for 24 hours raises a P3 work order, inside the band. |
| IT Partner SLA | FC-GPU | Before replacing a tray for a thermal slowdown, check the serving CDU's supply on the Telemetry of Record and attach it to the ticket. |

**Actions** (status as of Sep 10, 2026)

| ID | Action | Owner | Priority | Due | Status | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PA1 | Configure the setpoint-deviation alarm on every Hall A and Hall B CDU and change CDU filters on differential pressure, not only on the calendar. | Landlord Chief Engineer | P2 | 2026-10-15 | In progress | Replaying this history raises the alarm on CDU-A3 within its first warm week. |
| PA2 | Propose the FA-1 amendment through Interface Agreement change control. | Customer Site Lead | P2 | 2026-10-31 | Not started | Amendment signed by all three parties. |
| PA3 | Add the CDU supply check to the thermal slowdown runbook and train the night and day crews. | IT Partner Site Manager | P3 | 2026-09-30 | In progress | Every thermal slowdown ticket after the training carries the CDU reading. |

## P2. Optic lot LOT-2544 fails at 4.8 times the rate of the other lots

*Signal:* Optic module failure (DOM alarm) · *Grouped by:* Optic lot · *Failures:* Mar 2 to Aug 26 · *p* < 0.000001 (threshold 0.005) · *Owner (Interface Agreement RACI, Back-end fabric optics, cables, and fiber):* Customer (accountable), IT Partner (does the work)

**What the data shows**

- LOT-2544 is 14% of the installed optic modules and 42% of module failures: 47 failures against 14.8 expected, 4.8× the rate of the other lots.
- The failures are spread across 24 of 32 racks and both ends of the link (24 host side, 23 switch side).
- 583 of the lot's 632 modules are still installed; none of the lot is in the spares pool.

**Root cause.** Modules from LOT-2544 are 14% of the installed base and 42% of module failures: 47 failures, against 14.8 expected. They fail at both ends of the link (24 on the host side, 23 on the switch side) and across 24 of the 32 racks, so this is not one rack's handling, cabling, or cleaning. That points to the lot itself. It is a probable cause until the manufacturer's failure analysis confirms it.

**Cost.** 47 tickets and 184 link-hours down; 583 of the lot's 632 modules are still installed.

**Lesson.** Ticket counts by rack would never have shown this, because the lot is spread across the hall. Failures have to be grouped by what they have in common, including the lot, not just by where they happened.

**Standard-work changes**

| Document | Clause | Change |
|---|---|---|
| IT Partner SLA | FC-LINK | Record the module serial and lot on every optic replacement and send it to the Customer's asset inventory. |

**Actions** (status as of Sep 10, 2026)

## P3. Reseats do not fix XID 79 faults

*Signal:* XID 79 (GPU has fallen off the bus) · *Grouped by:* Fix applied · *Failures:* Mar 3 to Aug 10 · *p* < 0.000001 (threshold 0.003) · *Owner (Interface Agreement RACI, Compute tray (GPU, CPU, memory, cold plate)):* Customer (accountable), IT Partner (does the work)

**What the data shows**

- 17 of 23 'Cleaned/reseated' repairs came back within 30 days (median 12 days later), against 7.5% for every other repair: 9.9× the rate.
- 'Hardware replaced' for the same fault: 5 of 42 came back.
- Counted only for repairs with a full 30 days left in the window to show a recurrence.

**Root cause.** 17 of 23 reseats for XID 79 (GPU has fallen off the bus) came back within 30 days, a median of 12 days later, against 7.5% for every other repair. Replacing the tray for the same fault held: 5 of 42 came back. A reseat clears the symptom long enough to pass validation but does not fix whatever takes the GPU off the bus.

**Cost.** 24 tickets and 97 tray-hours out of service on 18 trays.

**Lesson.** Passing validation is not the same as holding. A fix that is cheaper at the time costs more when it fails twice, so a fix type needs its own recurrence rate, not just the ticket's.

**Standard-work changes**

| Document | Clause | Change |
|---|---|---|
| IT Partner SLA | FC-GPU | For XID 79, a reseat may close the ticket only once per tray; a second XID 79 within 30 days requires a tray replacement and an RMA. |
| IT Partner SLA | TR-5 | Report the 30-day recurrence rate for each fault class and fix type in the monthly service review. |

**Actions** (status as of Sep 10, 2026)

| ID | Action | Owner | Priority | Due | Status | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PA6 | Stop reseat-only closes for XID 79 while the rule card change goes through. | IT Partner Site Manager | P1 | 2026-09-30 | In progress | No XID 79 ticket closed as reseated after the date of this review. |
| PA7 | Amend FC-GPU through SLA change control and add fix-type recurrence to the monthly scorecard. | Customer Site Lead | P2 | 2026-10-31 | Not started | Rule card amended; the October scorecard shows recurrence by fix type. |

## Watch items

Groups with at least 5 failures and 2 times the rate of the rest that chance could still explain once the number of tests is accounted for. With 551 tests, about 6 would reach p < 0.01 by chance alone.

| Group | Observed | Expected by chance | Rate vs. the rest | p | Ruling |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Link fault with no module alarm (fiber or connector) on rack A30 | 6 links | 1.4 | 4.7× | 0.003 | Inspect. 7 link faults with no module alarm on 6 links in one rack is the most likely of the three to be real: ask the IT Partner to inspect A30's fiber trays and patching, and look again next review. |
| XID 79 (GPU has fallen off the bus) on rack A25 | 6 trays | 1.7 | 3.8× | 0.007 | No common factor: 6 faults on 6 different trays, none of them reseats, and only 1 a repeat. Look again next review. |
| Optic module failure (DOM alarm) on rack A01 | 9 modules | 3.5 | 2.7× | 0.009 | Not explained by the lot pattern: only 3 of the 9 failed modules are from LOT-2544. Look again next review. |

## Method

- **Failures come from the Telemetry of Record**, never from ticket text: DCGM (XIDs and thermal slowdowns), UFM (link down, and transceiver DOM alarms that name the failed module), and Redfish (PSU health). 496 failures, each matched to the ticket that repaired it (496 matched); the ticket supplies only the fix applied.
- **Groups.** Each failure signature by rack, by the racks a CDU serves, by tray slot, and by optic lot; every failure together by rack and by CDU; each signature by fix (does a reseat or clean hold for 30 days?); and GPU thermal slowdowns in the racks a CDU serves while that CDU ran warm (daily mean 1.0 °C or more above setpoint for at least 7 days).
- **Tests.** Location and lot: exact binomial test of the group's share of failing units against its share of the installed base (a unit that fails again counts once; repeat failures on one unit are CSL-08 and KM-09's job). Fix: one-sided Fisher exact test of 30-day recurrence against every other repair.
- **A pattern** needs at least 5 failures, 2 times the rate of the rest, and p under 0.05 divided by the number of tests in its family (Bonferroni): facility condition 0.050 (1 test), location 0.000096 (522 tests), asset lot 0.005 (10 tests), fix 0.003 (18 tests).
- **Owner.** The component's row in the Interface Agreement RACI. A thermal pattern explained by the CDU is the Landlord's (DM-COOL: the Landlord owns the CDUs and the header up to the rack manifold valves).
- **Judgment** (root cause, lessons, standard-work changes, actions) is written by people in `patterns/lessons.yaml` and tested against these facts: every number must match and no individual is named.

*Synthetic data for a portfolio demonstration; all names and events are fictional.*
